quarterly_data.signal: Record Q4 FY2026 (Jeff Clarke / David Kennedy): Q4 revenue was $33,400,000,000, up 39%, and EPS $3.89, up 45%; ISG revenue was a record $19,600,000,000, up 73% (eight consecutive quarters of double-digit growth), with ISG operating margin of 14.8%, up 240 basis points sequentially. Full-year FY2026 revenue reached $113,500,000,000, up 19%, and EPS grew 27% to $10.30. Starting this quarter Dell breaks out AI server revenue from the overall server and networking line.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $33,400,000,000, up 39%; EPS $3.89, up 45%; ISG revenue $19,600,000,000, up 73%; ISG operating margin 14.8%; FY 2026 revenue $113,500,000,000, up 19%, EPS $10.30

quarterly_data.signal: AI server records in Q4 (David Kennedy): $34,100,000,000 in orders, $9,500,000,000 in shipments, $9,000,000,000 in revenue and an ending backlog of $43,000,000,000; the five-quarter pipeline grew sequentially even after converting those orders. Full-year FY2026 AI orders were $64,100,000,000 with $25,200,000,000 shipped; orders grew six times over the previous year. Management says AI servers run at a mid-single-digit operating margin and that the backlog 'will ship at mid single digits'. Shipments vs revenue differ only by in-transit gear at quarter end.

Initial FY2027 guidance (David Kennedy): about $50,000,000,000 in AI revenue (about 100% growth), reflecting backlog composition, customer readiness and delivery schedules; total revenue $138,000,000,000 to $142,000,000,000, up 23% at the midpoint of $140,000,000,000; traditional servers and storage up mid-single digits (first-half weighted); CSG up roughly 1%; operating income up approximately 18%; non-GAAP EPS $12.90, plus or minus $0.25. Q1 FY2027 guide: revenue $34,700,000,000 to $35,700,000,000, up 51% at the midpoint, with ISG up over 100% on $13,000,000,000 of AI server revenue. Jeff Clarke: the $50,000,000,000 reflects customers' building/power build-outs and 'the availability of DRAM and E1 drives and E3 drives', and Dell is 'out looking for more parts'.

Traditional servers: demand significantly outpaced supply in Q4 with strong double-digit demand growth across every region; traditional server and networking revenue was $5,900,000,000, up 27%. Customers shifted to dense 16th/17th-generation configurations with more CPU, DRAM and storage; upgrading 14G to 17G consolidates at 'six to one to seven to one' (7:1), and a majority of the install base remains on 14th generation or older. AI workloads on x86 are picking up at 'AI-forward' enterprises. For FY2027 (calendar 2026) Jeff Clarke expects server 'units are clearly down, while TRUs are up', with second-half guidance kept prudent because of supply uncertainty.
quarterly_data.figure: traditional server and networking revenue $5,900,000,000, up 27%; 7:1 consolidation from 14G to 17G

quarterly_data.signal: CSG (PCs): revenue up 14% to $13,500,000,000; commercial up 16% to $11,600,000,000 (sixth consecutive quarter of growth); consumer roughly flat at $1,900,000,000; CSG operating income $600,000,000, or 4.7% of revenue, reflecting deliberate share capture (business grew 18% in a market that grew 10%) before a price increase on January 6. For FY2027 David Kennedy sees the PC market 'in around that minus 11%, minus 12% range', more acute in the second half, and guides CSG to 1% revenue growth.
quarterly_data.figure: CSG revenue $13,500,000,000, up 14%; commercial $11,600,000,000, up 16%; consumer $1,900,000,000; CSG operating income $600,000,000, or 4.7% of revenue; FY 2027 PC market minus 11%, minus 12%

quarterly_data.signal: Vera Rubin status at the start of FY2027: 'There is no Vera Rubin in the backlog' (the $43,000,000,000 AI backlog is 'overwhelmingly' Grace Blackwell), but 'There is Vera Rubin in the five-quarter pipeline'. Dell has 'early engineering samples' and forward-deployed engineers are working with customers on designs; Jeff Clarke expects it 'to ship in the second half of the year because we know Vera Rubin is in production'. Management expects a smoother transition than Grace Blackwell thanks to manufacturing and test lessons, while keeping AI operating margin in the mid single digits through the transition.
quarterly_data.figure: no Vera Rubin in the $43,000,000,000 AI backlog; shipments expected in the second half of the year

quarterly_data.signal: Blackwell mix (Q&A, David Kennedy / Jeff Clarke): the $43,000,000,000 AI backlog is 'predominantly—overwhelmingly—Grace Blackwell'. The largest share of the five-quarter pipeline is Grace Blackwell and Blackwell, with 'a rise in x86 Blackwell' driven primarily by enterprise deployments where 'air cooling' is the number one consideration, plus scientific computing and high-frequency traders using x86 air-cooled solutions.

players.product: PowerEdge XE9680 AI servers & PowerScale storage

quarterly_data.signal: Memory/NAND cost shock (Jeff Clarke): the DRAM spot market 'over the last six months is up nearly five and a half times at $2.39 a gigabit', and NAND 'is $0.20 a gigabyte', 'up nearly four times over the last six months' (he also cited industry-analyst estimates of further Q2-Q4 increases, not Dell's own). Dell has LTAs and capacity agreements in place with its memory partners, repriced its entire server business on December 10 and tens of thousands of open PC quotes on January 6, is moving to discount-off-list pricing with the shortest quote validity ever, and names securing supply as the first priority. The FY2027 AI guide is bounded partly by 'the availability of DRAM and E1 drives and E3 drives'.
quarterly_data.figure: DRAM spot $2.39 a gigabit (up nearly five and a half times in six months); NAND $0.20 a gigabyte (up nearly four times in six months)

quarterly_data.signal: Storage: revenue was $4,800,000,000, up 2%, with double-digit demand growth across the Dell IP portfolio (PowerMax, PowerStore, PowerScale, ObjectScale, data protection); all-flash arrays posted a third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and PowerStore an eighth consecutive quarter of growth (seven double digit). Half of the new customers being won are new to PowerStore and nearly 30% are new to Dell buying storage. Lightning, the parallel file solution, remains on track for general availability in the first half with early deployments underway. Management pitches PowerStore's five to one data reduction and up to 75 to one data-protection compression as ways to help customers through the 'memory crisis' with fewer servers and drives; Dell IP storage is expected to be a greater share of mix in FY2027 and is margin accretive.
quarterly_data.figure: storage revenue $4,800,000,000, up 2%; PowerStore data reduction five to one; data protection up to 75 to one

quarterly_data.signal: AI customer breadth: the AI customer base surpassed 4,000, with growth across neo clouds, sovereigns and enterprise; the five-quarter pipeline grew across CSPs, sovereigns, neo clouds and enterprise, and enterprise was 'the fastest-growing portion of the five-quarter pipeline', and Jeff Clarke called Q4 'a record quarter in enterprise revenue'. Dell declined to split AI orders by customer type. AI server attach centres on storage, networking and deployment/break-fix services.
